name: What is the difference between a custom spa and a prefab hot tub?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a custom spa and a prefab hot tub?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a custom spa and a prefab hot tub?

acceptedAnswer.text: A custom spa is designed around the property and the homeowner’s goals, so it can be sized, shaped, tiled, and integrated with surrounding hardscape in a way that fits the home. A prefab hot tub is a factory-made product with fixed dimensions, shell shape, jet layout, and cabinet style. Custom construction gives more control over seating, spillovers, waterline tile, coping, lighting, and how the spa connects to a pool or patio. Prefab units are typically faster to install and may cost less upfront, but they offer fewer design options and can look less tailored in luxury settings. For Los Angeles properties where outdoor living is part of the architecture, custom spas are often chosen for aesthetics, resale appeal, and better site integration. The decision usually comes down to budget, timeline, maintenance preferences, and how important a seamless architectural look is to the homeowner.
acceptedAnswer.description: A custom spa is built to fit a specific site, style, and equipment plan, while a prefab hot tub is a manufactured unit delivered mostly complete. Custom spas offer more design flexibility, but prefab units usually install faster and with fewer construction trades.
